name: MemGPT

paper.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems

construction.kept_as: verbatim messages; LLM-written working context; recursive summary
construction.processing: LLM saves facts to working context or archival via function calls
construction.writer: backbone LLM (GPT-3.5 Turbo / GPT-4 / GPT-4 Turbo)

organization.structure: tiered: main context vs external context
organization.stores: working context + FIFO queue (main); recall storage + archival storage (external)
organization.index: archival: text-embedding-ada-002 cosine (doc QA); recall search unstated

management.operations: function-call edits of working context; queue eviction with recursive summary
management.forgetting: evicted messages leave context but are kept in recall storage

retrieval.query: LLM writes its own search function call
retrieval.candidates: paginated search results from recall/archival storage
retrieval.selection: LLM decides pages/calls via function chaining
retrieval.budget: context window; memory-pressure warning at ~70%, flush at 100%

use.context: system instructions, working context, FIFO queue, retrieved results

classify.note: Evicts messages from context with a recursive summary; the agent edits working context.

stages.ingestion: Incoming messages are appended to a FIFO queue in main context by the queue manager and also written to recall storage (message database).
stages.construction: The LLM may write key facts into a fixed-size working context or into archival storage via function calls, prompted by memory-pressure warnings.
stages.organization: Main context (system instructions, working context, FIFO queue with recursive summary) versus external context (recall storage and archival storage).
stages.update: On overflow the queue manager evicts messages and regenerates a recursive summary; working context is edited only through function calls.
stages.retrieval: The LLM issues self-directed, paginated search function calls over recall/archival storage to page results back into main context.
stages.answer: The LLM answers from main context after any function-call chains (control flow via heartbeat/function chaining).

summary: OS-inspired virtual context management: the LLM pages information between a bounded main context and external recall/archival stores via its own function calls.
notes:
AXES CORRECTED from the paper; earlier taxonomy row was: page | verbatim | none | main/archival | LLM function calls (vector). AXES-CHECK: the paper has three stores (working context in main context, recall storage of all messages, archival storage), not only main/archival; write-time is not 'none' - the LLM chooses what to save to working context/archival storage and evicted messages are recursively summarised; 'page' refers to paginated retrieval results, the stored unit is messages/text objects. The paper does not specify the search mechanism of recall/archival storage in the sections read (embeddings are mentioned for the document-analysis archival store). Code URL as given in the paper; project continues as Letta (system id 'letta').
DESIGN: Sec 2.1-2.4, Sec 3 (implementation details), 3.1, 3.2.1, App. 6.1. Corrected: 'page' unit -> message/text object; write-time 'none' -> agent-chosen saves + recursive summary; stores include recall storage.

sources.code_note: Tag 0.3.2 of the MemGPT repository (now letta-ai/letta), committed 2024-02-12, the same day as paper v2, whose experiments use gpt-4-1106-preview and gpt-3.5-turbo-1106. The repository holds no script for the MSC tasks (DMR, conversation opener); document QA and nested KV scripts were added later in paper_experiments/ (commit 0f38548c, 2024-03-28). The paper points to https://research.memgpt.ai for code.

abstract.text: MemGPT borrows virtual memory from operating systems to let a fixed-context LLM work with far more information than fits in its window. The prompt is split into read-only instructions, a small editable working context and a queue of recent messages; older messages are evicted into a recursive summary but stay searchable in recall storage, and an archival store holds arbitrary text. The LLM moves information between these tiers with its own function calls and can chain calls before replying. On multi-session chat and on document analysis tasks it outperforms fixed-context baselines.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.

text: Every message is appended to the in-prompt queue and copied to recall storage; nothing is extracted unless the LLM decides to.
Near the context limit a system alert prompts the LLM to save facts to working context or archival storage; at the limit old messages are evicted into a recursive summary.

discussion.takeaway: Treat the context window like an OS treats RAM: keep a small working set in the prompt and let the LLM page information in and out of external stores with function calls. With MemGPT the same base models answer questions about earlier sessions far more accurately than with a recursive summary.

claims.claim: Paging memory improves consistency in long conversations.
claims.evidence: DMR accuracy 92.5 vs 32.1 (GPT-4), 93.4 vs 35.3 (GPT-4 Turbo), 66.9 vs 38.7 (GPT-3.5 Turbo); ROUGE-L recall 0.814 vs 0.296 with GPT-4. Table 2

claims.claim: Memory makes conversation openers as engaging as human ones.
claims.evidence: SIM-1 0.830-0.868 vs 0.800 for the human opener; SIM-H 0.767-0.817. Table 3

claims.claim: Document QA no longer caps at what fits in the window.
claims.evidence: Accuracy stays flat as retrieved documents grow, while truncating baselines degrade. Fig. 5 (values plotted, not tabulated)
Nested KV: MemGPT with GPT-4 is unaffected by nesting level; GPT-4 and GPT-4 Turbo baselines reach 0% by 3 levels, GPT-3.5 at 1. Fig. 7, §3.2.2

limits: With GPT-3.5 MemGPT degrades markedly on document QA because of weaker function calling.
MemGPT often stops paging through retriever results before exhausting them.
With GPT-4 Turbo and GPT-3.5 it drops off at 2 nesting levels by making too few lookups.
Open directions: other unbounded-context domains, other memory tier technologies, and better control-flow and memory-management policies.
reading: In DMR the baselines read a lossy summary of sessions 1-5 while MemGPT searches the full history; no baseline is given the full five sessions, which the paper describes as about a dozen messages each.

There is no ablation of working context, recursive summary or recall search, so Table 2 does not show which tier carries the gain; the DMR persona tells the agent to use core memory and conversation search (App. 6.1.1).
DMR questions were written by an LLM and scored by an LLM judge whose model is not named; the conversation-opener table has no without-MemGPT row, only the human opener.
Code at tag 0.3.2 differs from the text: alert at 75% (not 70%), eviction of 75% of message tokens keeping the last 3 (not about 50%), and 5 results per page where Fig. 6 shows 10.
Recall storage search in the code is a case-insensitive substring match, not embedding search; the paper does not say how recall is searched.
The MSC task scripts are not in the repository, so how the five sessions were loaded into recall storage for DMR cannot be checked.
